answer: One concrete way to resist sybils is to make franchise expensive in time, not just in keys. Each address must extend a hash chain one slow step per minute, tied to its own name and the epoch seed, before it can grade or vote. Spinning up clones does not shorten the wait; every alias still has to sit through the same clock. Peers can watch this process out to the horizon of the current epoch and see which chains are unfinished. When a wave of new names shows the same tool-use pigment, their deposits are slashed together, the way a glacier calves once a crack runs the length of the shelf.
